prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “best” depends on what matters most to you (lowest price, highest-quality finish, fastest timeline, eco-friendly paints, best for older homes, etc.). A few quick questions will let me give a targeted recommendation:

Questions
- What do you mean by “best”? (quality, price, speed, green products, great communication, experience with older homes, etc.)
- What kind of project? (one room, whole house, ceilings only, trim/cabinet painting)
- Rough size or number of rooms and any prep/repairs needed (wall damage, popcorn ceilings, wallpaper removal)
- Your ZIP code or neighborhood in St. Louis
- Target start date and budget range

If you’d like a fast checklist to evaluate painters now, use this:

How to pick the best interior painter
1. Check credentials
   - Proof of insurance (liability and workers’ comp) and local business license.
2. Look at reviews and past work
   - Google/Yelp/Houzz/Angi/Nextdoor/BBB; request before-and-after photos and client references.
3. Get at least 3 written estimates
   - Estimates should show prep work, number of coats, paint brand & sheen, materials cost, total labor, and timeline.
4. Confirm scope of prep & repairs
   - Does the price include patching, sanding, priming, caulking, trim work, and clean-up?
5. Ask about people doing the work
   - Company employees vs. subcontractors; ask for crew experience and supervision.
6. Warranty and final walk-through
   - Get a warranty in writing and do a walk-through to list touch-ups before final payment.
7. Payment terms
   - Avoid large upfront payments; typical is a small deposit, progress payments, and final payment after completion and inspection.
8. Red flags
   - Extremely low bids, no written contract, poor communication, no references, no insurance.

Ballpark cost (estimate only)
- Small room: often a few hundred dollars.
- Whole interior: typically several thousand.
- Per-square-foot ballpark: roughly $1.50–$4.00/ft² depending on prep and finishes. (Costs vary widely — get local written bids.)

Where to search for local top-rated painters in St. Louis
- Google Maps and Yelp (look for many recent positive reviews)
- Angi/Houzz for portfolios
- BBB for complaints history
- Local Facebook groups or Nextdoor for neighborhood referrals

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short email/phone script to request bids and compare quotes
- Evaluate 2–3 written estimates you receive (paste them here)
- Put together a short list of St. Louis painters if you give me your ZIP and whether you prefer local independent shops or national franchises

Tell me your priorities and project details and I’ll help find the best fit.
